question: Prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion among ADNI MCI participants from MRI plus cognitive tests. Same task and population class. The shared channels are MRI and cognitive testing (P-183: T2-map signal/texture, volumes and neuropsychology; P-186: FreeSurfer MRI markers and neuropsychological measures). Allowed differences: label definition, single baseline vs two observed visits plus a forecast value, imaging features, age range, sample size and validation design.
metric: AUC with AUC (0.824 vs 0.957; P-186's 6-month-ahead analysis gives 0.912).

figures.P-183: Ensemble AUC 0.824, reported 95% CI 0.681-0.968; n=40 (18 MCIp, 22 MCIs); 100 random 80/20 splits; best of seven methods. Neuropsychology-only best AUC 0.727, reported 95% CI 0.567-0.888 (LASSO, Table 3).
figures.P-186: NM+MRI, 1-year-ahead: AUC 0.957, 5-fold CV, n=85 (35 MCIp, 50 MCIs); no interval reported. Hanley-McNeil with n1=35, n2=50: Q1=0.9175, Q2=0.9360, SE=0.0249, 95% CI 0.908-1.000 (capped). 6-month-ahead: AUC 0.912, n=119 (49/70), SE=0.0297, 95% CI 0.854-0.970. NM-only 1-year-ahead: AUC 0.915 (Table 5), SE=0.0347, 95% CI 0.847-0.983.
figures.comparison: P-183's 0.824 lies outside both of P-186's derived intervals (0.908-1.000 and 0.854-0.970). P-186's 0.957 and 0.912 lie inside P-183's reported interval 0.681-0.968. The rule's test (one estimate outside the other's interval) is met, in one direction. On the neuropsychology-only subset, each estimate lies outside the other's interval: 0.915 is above P-183's 0.888 upper bound, and 0.727 is below P-186's 0.847 lower bound.

matched_figure_check: No figure is reported under the other paper's condition. P-186 has no baseline-only or single-visit result: every figure uses two observed visits plus a forecast third value, and its ground-truth figures use three observed visits. P-183 has no longitudinal result. The one shared-subset comparison, neuropsychology only, does not reconcile the pair; the gap there is wider (0.727 vs 0.915). Condition 3 holds.
performance_validity: Passes condition 5 on the compared figures: 0.957 (n=85, internal 5-fold CV, no external cohort) is below the 0.97 threshold, and 0.824 is well below. P-186's ground-truth AUC of 0.98 (Table 5) uses observed future values and is not the compared figure. P-186 normalises all features before the train-test split, ranks markers by t-tests on baseline readings, and reports the best marker-subset size, so its 0.957 is optimistic. This is recorded as a candidate explanation, not an exclusion.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation: P-186 classifies three-point trajectories, two observed visits plus a forecast value at the time of conversion; P-183 uses one baseline visit. P-186 attributes its AUC mainly to the forecast value but reports no two-visit-only or baseline-only comparator, so this is not shown to be sufficient.
candidate_explanations.quote: method proposed in this paper has recorded the highest classiﬁcation AUC of 95.7% predominantly because of involving the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classiﬁcation feature.

candidate_explanations.difference: Baseline-only input and age restriction in P-183.
candidate_explanations.quote: The experiment included only the baseline information from subjects with a baseline MCI diagnosis, between 70 and 80 years old

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition: P-183 uses an extreme-group design (conversion at the 2-year visit vs stability for at least 5 years); P-186 counts conversion at any time before month 36 against MCI throughout.
candidate_explanations.quote: converting to AD any time before the last follow-up time, i.e., 36th month, are called MCI progressors (MCIp)

candidate_explanations.difference: Imaging features: quantitative T2 relaxometry maps (signal and texture) in P-183 vs FreeSurfer morphometric markers in P-186.
candidate_explanations.quote: In order to generate the T2 maps, we used the dual fast spin-echo images, namely, the PD- and T2-weighted images

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation optimism in P-186: features scaled on the whole dataset before splitting, markers ranked on baseline readings, and the reported marker-subset size chosen from the results. P-183 reports the best of seven methods over repeated 80/20 splits.
candidate_explanations.quote: We scale all features to have values between 0 and 1 before the train-test split.

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size and eligibility: n=40 aged 70-80 (P-183) vs n=85 ADNI-1 MCI with three consecutive annual readings (P-186).
candidate_explanations.quote: for 1-year-ahead prediction, the dataset contains three consecutive annual readings, resulting in 35 MCIp and 50 MCIs subjects

reason: Both papers predict MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI from MRI plus cognitive tests and report AUC. P-183's 0.824 lies outside the intervals derived for P-186's 0.957 (0.908-1.000) and 0.912 (0.854-0.970), and neither paper reports a result under the other's input condition that would reconcile them. The pair qualifies under the rule as written, but the uncertainty test holds in one direction only: P-183's own interval (0.681-0.968, n=40) contains both of P-186's figures. The candidate explanations (P-186's forecast-value input, the label definitions, the imaging features, P-186's optimistic validation, and sample size) are not shown to be sufficient.
